name: Question 3
problem: A fair seven-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $7$ is thrown once. If $X$ is the outcome of the die, what is the variance of $X?$
worked_solution:
The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $7$ possible outcomes ($1,2,3,4,5,6,7$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ |

Now, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6)+7\cdot f(7) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{7})+2(\frac{1}{7})+3(\frac{1}{7})+4(\frac{1}{7})+5(\frac{1}{7})+6(\frac{1}{7})+7(\frac{1}{7}) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=4$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-4)^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =(1-4)^{2}\cdot f(1)+(2-4)^{2}\cdot f(2)+(3-4)^{2}\cdot f(3)+(4-4)^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & +(5-4)^{2}\cdot f(5)+(6-4)^{2}\cdot f(6)+(7-4)^{2}\cdot f(7) \\  & =9\cdot f(1)+4\cdot f(2)+1\cdot f(3)+0\cdot f(4)+1\cdot f(5)+2\cdot f(6)+9\cdot f(7) \\  & =9(\frac{1}{7})+4(\frac{1}{7})+1(\frac{1}{7})+0+1(\frac{1}{7})+4(\frac{1}{7})+9(\frac{1}{7}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The variance of a discrete random variable X with probability mass function f(x) defined over a set S is given by

Var[X]=∑x∈S(x−E[X])2⋅f(x).

First, we need to compute the probability mass function f(x). Here, there are 7 possible outcomes (1,2,3,4,5,6,7) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

x 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
f(x) 17 17 17 17 17 17 17

Now, we need to compute E[X]. Summing up the products of each value of X and its associated probability, we get

E[X]=1⋅f(1)+2⋅f(2)+3⋅f(3)+4⋅f(4)+5⋅f(5)+6⋅f(6)+7⋅f(7)=1(17)+2(17)+3(17)+4(17)+5(17)+6(17)+7(17)=4.

Substituting E[X]=4 into the variance formula, we get

Var[X]=∑x∈S(x−4)2⋅f(x).

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

Var[X]=(1−4)2⋅f(1)+(2−4)2⋅f(2)+(3−4)2⋅f(3)+(4−4)2⋅f(4)==+(5−4)2⋅f(5)+(6−4)2⋅f(6)+(7−4)2⋅f(7)=9⋅f(1)+4⋅f(2)+1⋅f(3)+0⋅f(4)+1⋅f(5)+2⋅f(6)+9⋅f(7)=9(17)+4(17)+1(17)+0+1(17)+4(17)+9(17)=4
